content.text:
Fixed and proven — all 3 tests pass.

The bug was in `cart.py:2`: `return sum(items) + items[-1]`. Since `sum(items)` already includes every item, adding `items[-1]` counted the last item a second time. The fix is simply `return sum(items)`.

Proof with tests (run via `uvx pytest`, since the active venv has no pytest):

- **Before the fix**, the existing test failed exactly as the bug predicts: `total([1, 2, 3])` returned 9 instead of 6 (the trailing 3 counted twice).
- **After the fix**, that test passes, along with two I added to pin the behavior down: `test_total_single_item_not_doubled` (`total([5]) == 5` — under the bug this returned 10, the sharpest demonstration of the double-count) and `test_total_empty` (`total([]) == 0` — the old code would have raised `IndexError` on `items[-1]`, so the fix also removes an empty-cart crash).
